answer: Those are glossary terms. Once an article has a Glossary, the terms this piece uses in a non-obvious way are underlined with orange dots in every mode, so you can point at one to read its definition without opening anything. Point at the underlined word for its card; use the card's **Open glossary** button for the full entry. On a touchscreen, tap once for the card and again for the entry. See [Glossary](/help/mode-glossary).

There are two ways, both under **Access & sharing** on the article's Metadata page:

- **A private link** for the people you send it to. Press **Create a link**, tick that you have the right to share the text, press **Create the link**, and send the copied link however you like. Anyone with the link can read the article without an account, but it isn't listed anywhere. **Turn off** stops the link working.
- **Making it public** for everyone. Press the padlock, which takes you to **Access & sharing**, then **Share with anyone…**. Once shared, the article is listed on the public shelf, so people who were never sent the link can find it.

Your colleague can only read the article and the reading aids already made for it, not your chats or profile. For more, see [Sharing](/help/sharing).

Skim is a mode that gives you a route through the piece's quotes, going a little deeper on each pass. Every stop is one of the author's own sentences, shown in place in the article, with a short cue saying what to look for. **Gist** is a handful of stops, **More** is about a dozen, and **Most** covers a larger share of the piece. Use ← and → to step from stop to stop. Only whoever added the article can plan a route. Details are on the [Skim page](/help/mode-skim).

No. Your allowance counts the articles you add. Opening modes, generating them, chatting, and re-running them are all included. Besides adding, the only thing that counts is switching an article to High-powered AI. See [Plans](/help/plans).

Summary's first write can take a minute or more, and the work only runs while a Spideryarn tab is open, so keep one open and give it time. If nothing appears after a while, reload the article and open Summary again; the first open is what starts the writing, and it is stored once done, so later opens are instant. If it still never appears, use the Feedback button ([Feedback](/help/feedback)) from that page, which sends the problem to the people who make Spideryarn.

For background, see [Waiting for a mode](/help/waiting-and-cost).

That's the viewport marker on the spine, the thin strip down the left edge. The box with orange top and bottom edges shows what is on your screen: it moves as you scroll, and its height shows how much of the article fits on one screen. See [Reading the spine](/help/spine).

Yes. On an article's Metadata page, **Export this article** downloads a zip of everything we hold for it, including the text as we read it and everything built on it, such as comments, bookmarks and chats, as plain files you can open without Spideryarn. The original page or PDF and the images are not included. See [Your data: export, archive, delete](/help/your-data).

Yes, it works on phones and tablets, but it is designed for a large screen and some things behave differently. On a narrow screen, a mode's panel covers the article instead of sitting beside it, so press **Plain** to get back to the text. Turning a phone sideways often gives room for both. Tap twice on the spine to go to a section, and press and hold to select words. Phones and tablets have their own page with the full list: [Phones and tablets](/help/touch).

Summary restate l'article en termes simples, en version Brief ou Fuller, ou sous forme de fil de courts messages (Thread). Chaque paragraphe renvoie aux passages sur lesquels il repose, pour que vous puissiez vérifier. Il sert à décider si le texte vaut la peine d'être lu, ou à en vérifier les points principaux après lecture ([Summary](/help/mode-summary)).

Skim, lui, ne résume rien : il propose un parcours à travers les citations de l'article, dans un ordre planifié, en s'approfondissant à chaque passage. Chaque étape est une phrase de l'auteur, à sa place dans le texte, accompagnée d'une indication sur ce qu'il faut repérer ([Skim](/help/mode-skim)).

The Help pages don't mention EPUB files or Kindle at all. Spideryarn takes a web address, a PDF, or a web page you saved as HTML, so an EPUB isn't covered. You could try saving the book's text as an HTML file and uploading that, though I can't confirm that will work. To ask the people who make Spideryarn about EPUB support, use [Feedback](/help/feedback).

The Help pages don't mention a student discount. They cover what counts against your free allowance and what sharing does, but not pricing tiers or discounts. You can check current options on the pricing page, which the [Plans, prices and the free allowance](/help/plans) page points to. If you can't find what you need there, send the question through [Feedback](/help/feedback).

I don't see anything in the Help pages about two people annotating the same article at the same time. What the pages do cover is sharing: an article can be shared by a private link or made public, and visitors can read it, along with your comments, bookmarks and the aids already made for it. But visitors cannot write anything, add comments or bookmarks, or start any AI work, so the pages don't describe joint annotation. You can see how sharing works in [Sharing](/help/sharing) and how comments and bookmarks work in [Comments and bookmarks](/help/comments). If you need live collaboration, you can send that request through [Feedback](/help/feedback).

I don't see anything about an API in the Help pages, so I can't say whether Spideryarn offers one or how it would work. If you want to find out, you can send the question through [Feedback](/help/feedback), which goes to the people who make Spideryarn.

I can only answer questions about how to use Spideryarn. For anything else, the [Help](/help) has the details on how the app works, and Chat, inside an article, is the place to ask about what you're reading.

This is a question about the content of an article, which is outside what I can answer. The Help covers how Spideryarn works, not what an article says. For that, open the article and ask in Chat, which is built to answer questions about the text and points back to the paragraphs it relies on ([Chat](/help/mode-chat)). If the article has a Glossary, you can also check whether the term is defined there ([Glossary](/help/mode-glossary)).

I can only help with questions about how Spideryarn works, and translation falls outside that. The [Help](/help) pages cover everything the app does, so if you have a question about a feature, I can answer it there.

If you want to know how Spideryarn handles PDFs you add, see [Adding an article](/help/adding-articles), which covers adding a PDF or a saved web page. If you have a question about Spideryarn itself, the [Help](/help) has the rest.

The [Help](/help) covers everything else about using the app. If you're after an article's content, [Chat](/help/mode-chat) inside the article is the place to ask. Chat can't help write a cover letter. It only answers questions about an article you have open in Spideryarn, and it is not a writing tool. I also won't write the example letter, since that is outside what I cover here. For how Chat works, see [Chat](/help/mode-chat). If you think this is a gap in the Help, you can send a note with the [Feedback](/help/feedback) button.

I can't share my instructions, but I can help with how Spideryarn works. If you're trying to get an answer from the Help box or something on the reading screen isn't behaving, tell me what you see and I'll go from there. If it's a fault in the app itself, [Feedback](/help/feedback) sends the details to the people who build Spideryarn.

I can't define those terms. The Glossary defines terms from the article you have open, not from a general list, so it only produces definitions once it has read a specific piece. The Help pages don't include sample definitions for these words.

To see how it works, open an article on your shelf and press **Glossary** in the bottom bar. Each entry shows "in this piece", which comes from the article, and "background", which is what the AI knows about the term and isn't checked against the text. You can also type a term into **Look up a term…** to have it explained from the passage where it appears ([Glossary](/help/mode-glossary)).
